test_title: PYST 7: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - English (Held On: 14th Sep 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
**Find the part of the sentence containing an error:**

The policy intends to neither penalise minor offenders (1)/ nor those who unknowingly broke norms (2)/ due to unclear guidelines (3)/ rather than purposeful violation. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in the incorrect placement of the correlative conjunctions **neither…nor**.
 
• The sentence begins with **“The policy intends to neither…”**, which is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct structure is **“intends neither to penalise… nor to overlook…”** — the word **‘neither’** should come before the infinitive verb, not between “to” and the verb.
 
• Thus, the grammatical error appears in **Part 1**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“The policy intends neither to penalise minor offenders nor those who unknowingly broke norms due to unclear guidelines rather than purposeful violation.”* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Part 2:** “nor those who unknowingly broke norms” — grammatically correct and properly connected with “nor”.
 
• **Part 3:** “due to unclear guidelines” — correctly describes the cause; no error.
 
• **Part 4:** “rather than purposeful violation.” — structurally correct as a contrast phrase.
